slots.rule: The arrears journey that goes deepest: missed payment, notices, then repaid, written off or passed to an agency
slots.glossary: The debt journey: a bill goes unpaid, then reminders and a payment plan follow, and it ends repaid, written off or with a collection agency.
slots.reason: No household in this run passes this example's checks yet. 599 households match the rule, and each fails at least one check an energy reader would apply: its bills carry no due date, so its payment record cannot count a payment missed (599 of 599); its story says the debt is cleared while its own balance at that moment is still owed past due (522 of 599); its record places the debt with an agency, and no moment of the story shows it (153 of 599); its account id is not in the public format (125 of 599).

slots.rule: The household whose electric car moved its use the most, with the supplier's inference set against it
slots.glossary: An EV home: an electric car arrives, and the supplier sees it only as more electricity on the meter.
slots.reason: No household in this run passes this example's checks yet. 21 households match the rule, and each fails at least one check an energy reader would apply: it lacks a full year of electricity use either side of the car (16 of 21); the car's effect its record states is not the 1,750-3,300 kWh a year an EV adds (5 of 21); its electricity over the year after the car did not rise by the 1,750-3,300 kWh an EV adds (3 of 21); it pays by prepayment yet is sent estimated credit bills (3 of 21).

slots.rule: A two-rate (profile class 2) home billed on its meter's registers
slots.glossary: Storage heating: heaters that charge overnight on a two-rate meter (such as Economy 7), whose night units are billed cheaper.
slots.reason: No household in this run passes this example's checks yet. 95 households match the rule, and each fails at least one check an energy reader would apply: the record names no profile class 2 (Economy 7) meter for it (95 of 95); it has no full calendar year of electricity on record (34 of 95); it uses less electricity than a home that does not heat with it (27 of 95); it pays by prepayment yet is sent estimated credit bills (10 of 95).

slots.rule: The largest year-on-year rise in one month's bill through the 2022 crisis
slots.glossary: The 2022 shock: wholesale prices rose several times over, and the price cap and then the Energy Price Guarantee set what households paid.
slots.story: The 2022 crisis reaches one household's bill.
